text: This case study is an illustrative, fictional scenario, built to make a real and common failure pattern concrete -- not an account of any actual company. It's the direct payoff of Chapter 1's platform-as-a-product framing, not a new idea bolted on at the end of the course.

Northfield Retail's platform team spent two quarters building exactly what this course has taught: a Backstage-style catalog, a golden-path scaffolder template with CI/CD and monitoring pre-wired, GitOps-driven deploys through ArgoCD, and canary rollouts with automated rollback. By every technical measure, it worked.

Six months after launch, the architecture review still praised it and the demo was still clean -- but fewer than fifteen percent of the company's services had been onboarded, and most of those were onboarded because a director told the owning team to, not because the team chose to.

Three specific failures explain why. First, no feedback loop -- the platform was built in isolation, based on guesses about developer needs, so low adoption itself became the first real signal, arriving six months late. Second, adoption by mandate instead of earning it -- when leadership escalated, teams registered their catalog entry on paper while quietly keeping old deploy scripts running underneath, since the mandate covered registering, not actually using, the golden path.

Third, and deepest: the golden path itself was designed around the stateless services the platform team found comfortable, and it simply didn't fit Northfield's long-running batch jobs or its compliance-gated services. For those teams, the self-service path meant fighting a template built for the wrong shape of service, then filing a ticket anyway -- strictly worse than the process it was supposed to replace.

None of this needed new technology to fix -- it needed treating the platform as a product from the start: interviewing real teams before building, instrumenting adoption from day one per Chapter 7, earning adoption instead of mandating it, and building a second golden path for teams the first one never fit. Lesson 32 closes the loop, reviewing how every chapter in this course connects to that one lesson.
